extracted.intended_audience: college mathematics faculty, department chairs, and assessment coordinators involved in undergraduate program assessment
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and instruments for designing and implementing assessment of the undergraduate mathematics major (portfolio-based, capstone, comprehensive exams, diagnostics, surveys, focus groups). Includes a Teaching Goals Inventory and a worked example from a department using student portfolios.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaching Goals Inventory (TGI) — purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The Teaching Goals Inventory is a self-assessment of instructional goals. Its purpose is threefold: (1) to help college teachers become more aware of what they want to accomplish in individual courses; (2) to help faculty locate Classroom Assessment Techniques they can adapt and use to assess how well they are achieving their teaching and learning goals; and (3) to provide a starting point for discussion of teaching and learning goals among colleagues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directions: Select ONE course you are currently teaching and respond with that course in mind. Rate the importance of each of the fifty-two goals to that course using a 1-to-5 scale. Read through all 52 goals before rating. Scale: (5) Essential — a goal you always/nearly always try to achieve; (4) Very Important — you often try to achieve; (3) Important — sometimes; (2) Unimportant — rarely; (1) Not applicable — never. Use results for personal reflection, departmental discussion, and to link to appropriate Classroom Assessment Techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary role options: teaching students facts and principles; role model; higher-order thinking; preparing for careers; fostering development; helping learning skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 52 (and the following single-choice question): In general, how do you see your primary role as a teacher? Choose only one: 1 Teaching students facts and principles of the subject matter; 2 Providing a role model for students; 3 Helping students develop higher-order thinking skills; 4 Preparing students for jobs/careers; 5 Fostering student development and personal growth; 6 Helping students develop basic learning skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a forced-choice reflection on instructor priorities; rate/select the single best descriptor for your primary role when completing the TGI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Departmental goal (Columbia College): prepare majors for graduate school, secondary teaching, or math-related careers
rubrics_metrics.description: Goal: The Mathematics Department of Columbia College is committed to providing mathematics majors the coursework and experiences which will enable them to attend graduate school, teach at the secondary level or enter a mathematics related career in business, industry or government. It is expected that each mathematics major will be able to accomplish a set of objectives (listed below).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This departmental goal frames the portfolio-based assessment program and informs the specific measurable objectives and indicators used for evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective 1: Demonstrate the ability to write mathematical proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate the ability to write mathematical proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment criterion: Each student portfolio will contain at least four examples of proofs she has written in different classes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective 2: Demonstrate the ability to read and evaluate a statistical study
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate the ability to read and evaluate a statistical study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment criterion: Each student portfolio will contain an evaluation of a statistical study that she has completed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective 3: Demonstrate knowledge of women in mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate knowledge of women in mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment criterion: Each student portfolio will contain evidence of knowledge of the contributions of women to mathematics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective 4: Demonstrate topics in calculus from various perspectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate topics in calculus from numerical, graphical, analytical and verbal perspectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment criterion: Each student portfolio will contain at least one topic from calculus demonstrated from the numerical, graphical, analytical and verbal perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective 5: Use mathematics as a problem solving tool in real life situations
rubrics_metrics.description: Use mathematics as a problem solving tool in real life situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment criterion: Each student portfolio will contain at least four examples of her use of mathematics in solving a real life problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective 6: Work collaboratively to solve problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Work collaboratively to solve problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment criteria: (i) Each student portfolio will contain at least four examples of problems that the student has solved collaboratively and a reflective statement about the collaborative process; (ii) 75% of course syllabi in upper level courses will indicate learning activities requiring collaborative problem-solving and/or presentation of in-depth problem solving to the class; (iii) a team of students selected and trained by the mathematics faculty will participate in the nationwide COMAP contest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective 7: Organize, connect and communicate mathematical ideas effectively
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize, connect and communicate mathematical ideas effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment criterion: Each student portfolio will contain four examples with evidence of mathematical communication, either in written or spoken form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective 8: Use technology appropriately to explore mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: Use technology appropriately to explore mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment criterion: Each student portfolio will contain at least four examples of mathematical exploration using technology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective 9: Feel adequately prepared for post-graduation experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Feel adequately prepared for their post-graduation experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment criterion: 90% of math major graduates who respond to a graduate survey will indicate that they felt mathematically prepared for the job they hold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portfolio implementation requirements (Columbia College practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural requirements used to ensure portfolio creation and quality: designate certain courses as portfolio development courses; include orientation, checklists, required entries, and cover sheets requiring reflective writing; partially completed portfolios submitted and graded as part of courses; require completed portfolio submission as a condition for passing the mandatory senior capstone course.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementation notes: Initially portfolios were not produced without requirements. Making submission mandatory and integrating portfolio tasks into class time and graded work improved collection but required articulating explicit departmental goals so portfolios could be meaningfully evaluated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for explicit measurable goals (lesson from findings)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the absence of stated expectations for student work in portfolios, no conclusions could be reached; departmental goals must be specific and include student behaviors to allow meaningful evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical guidance: Craft clear goals and specific indicators before collecting artifacts; revise goals based on pilot readings of student work to ensure usefulness of portfolio evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance subjective portfolio evidence with objective instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: Because of small-department familiarity with students, portfolio evaluation risked subjectivity; an objective instrument (e.g., standardized test or other measures) is necessary to balance subjective findings from portfolios.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use mixed-method assessment: combine portfolios and reflective artifacts with surveys, diagnostics, standardized instruments, or rubrics applied blind to increase objectivity.
